caption: The drawing depicts a single spoon shown from three different perspectives using grayscale pencil shading. The first view, at the top, displays the spoon from a top-down angle, showing an oval-shaped bowl and a straight handle that widens and becomes squared off at the end. The second view, in the middle, presents the underside of the same spoon, with the bowl and handle mirroring the shape in the first view, but now with subtle changes in shading that indicate the concave bottom surface and the handle's reflective quality. The third view, at the bottom, shows the profile of the spoon from the side, revealing the depth of the bowl and the gentle upward curve of the handle. The drawing is executed on a light beige background with fine gradient pencil marks used to create the metallic appearance of the spoon, emphasizing highlights and shadows. The composition is centered on the page, with each view of the spoon spaced horizontally in a rectangular frame. There are artist's signatures and small notations near the bottom left and right of the sketch box.
title: Silver Tablespoon
